title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
paragraphs: Douglas Adams's BBC science-fiction comedy follows the bewildered Arthur Dent after Earth is destroyed, sending him across the galaxy with Ford Prefect and an increasingly improbable group of companions.

The frozen GRH container is the complete 32-Fit BBC radio sequence across six named phases: Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Quandary, Quintessential and Hexagonal. The first 12 Fits originate as radio drama; later phases adapt later novels. Frozen titles are book/part labels and are retained while canonical Fit aliases and original BBC dates are added as research evidence.

GRH documents the program through Primary Phase (March 8, 1978 to April 12, 1978) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]], Secondary Phase (December 24, 1978 to January 25, 1980) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]], Tertiary Phase (September 21, 2004 to October 26, 2004) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]], and Quandary Phase (May 3, 2005 to May 24, 2005) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Douglas Adams (source author on 14 recordings, writer on 12 recordings, and additional material on 6 recordings), Dirk Maggs (radio adaptor on 20 recordings and director on 20 recordings), Geoffrey McGivern (performer on 12 recordings), Paddy Kingsland (music on 12 recordings), Peter Jones (performer on 12 recordings), Simon Jones (performer on 12 recordings), and Geoffrey Perkins (producer on 11 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include interstellar travel and cosmic scale, The Hitchhiker's Guide and information systems, absurdist science-fiction comedy, and Earth, destruction and reconstruction.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including 1978 BBC Radio 4 science-fiction comedy launch, Secondary Phase completion, 2004-2005 radio revival and novel adaptations, and 2018 fortieth-anniversary Hexagonal Phase.
